title: Boat running upstream takes hours minutes to cover certain distance,
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A boat running upstream takes 8 hours 48 minutes to cover a certain distance, while it takes 4 hours to cover the same distance running towards downstream. Then the ratio between the speed of boat and the speed of the water current is
solution:
For boat-and-stream problems, downstream speed equals the boat's speed plus the current's speed, and upstream speed equals the boat's speed minus the current's speed. For a fixed distance covered in different times, speed = distance ÷ time, so the two given times fix the two speeds.

  1. Convert the upstream time to hours: 8 hours 48 minutes = 8 + 48/60 hours = 8 + 4/5 hours = 44/5 hours.

  2. Let the common distance be D. Downstream speed = D / 4.

  3. Upstream speed = D / (44/5) = 5D / 44.

  4. Boat speed = half the sum of the two speeds: (D/4 + 5D/44) / 2. Writing D/4 as 11D/44, the sum is 16D/44, so boat speed = 8D/44 = 2D/11.

  5. Current speed = half the difference of the two speeds: (11D/44 − 5D/44) / 2 = (6D/44) / 2 = 3D/44.

  6. Boat speed : current speed = (2D/11) : (3D/44) = (8D/44) : (3D/44) = 8 : 3.

Check: with boat speed = 8k and current speed = 3k, downstream speed = 11k and upstream speed = 5k, so the time ratio (upstream : downstream) = 1/5k : 1/11k = 11 : 5 = 8.8 hours : 4 hours — exactly the 8 hours 48 minutes and 4 hours given in the question, confirming the ratio.

optionFeedback.html: This is what you get by rounding 8 hours 48 minutes down to a plain 8 hours and comparing the two times directly as 8 : 4 — but 48 minutes is a real part of the upstream time, and a time ratio only becomes a speed ratio after it is inverted.

This ratio doesn't follow from correctly converting 8 hours 48 minutes into a fraction of an hour and forming the two speeds for the same distance — recheck the time conversion and the resulting calculation before locking in this ratio.

Once 8 hours 48 minutes is correctly converted to 44/5 hours, the half-sum and half-difference of the two resulting speeds give the boat and current speeds respectively, and their ratio is exactly 8 to 3.

This is typically chosen after a computational or unit-conversion slip during the speed calculation, which makes the resulting number feel unfamiliar — go back and recheck the time-to-hours conversion and the arithmetic before concluding the ratio isn't among the given choices.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2023 Q64
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A boat takes 19 hours for travelling downstream from point A to point B and coming back to a point C which is at midway between A and B. If the velocity of the stream is 4 kmph and the speed of the boat in still water is 14 km ph, what is the distance between A and B?
solution:
Concept

In still water a boat moves at its own speed. A stream adds its speed to the boat going downstream and takes it away going upstream, so downstream speed = speed in still water + speed of the stream, and upstream speed = speed in still water - speed of the stream.

The time for any leg of a journey = distance for that leg divided by the effective speed on that leg, and the time for a journey made of several legs is the sum of the individual leg times.

Application

Here the speed in still water is 14 kmph and the stream is 4 kmph, so the downstream speed is 14 + 4 = 18 kmph and the upstream speed is 14 - 4 = 10 kmph. Let the distance AB be d km.

  1. The outward leg from A to B is with the stream: it covers d km at 18 kmph, taking d/18 hours.

  2. C is the midpoint of AB, so the return leg from B to C covers d/2 km.

  3. That return leg is against the stream at 10 kmph, so it takes (d/2) / 10 = d/20 hours.

  4. The whole journey is given as 19 hours, so d/18 + d/20 = 19.

  5. Taking the LCM of 18 and 20, which is 180: 10d/180 + 9d/180 = 19d/180 = 19.

  6. Therefore 19d = 19 x 180, which gives d = 180.

Cross-check

Putting d = 180 km back into the journey: the downstream leg takes 180 / 18 = 10 hours and the 90 km upstream return takes 90 / 10 = 9 hours. Together that is 10 + 9 = 19 hours, exactly the time stated in the question, so the value is consistent.

Contrast

Total time here is directly proportional to AB, since the total works out to 19d/180 hours, so a shorter AB always gives a shorter total journey:

  • AB = 120 km gives a total of 12 2/3 hours.

  • AB = 140 km gives a total of 14 7/9 hours.

  • AB = 160 km gives a total of 16 8/9 hours.

The distance between A and B is 180 km.

optionFeedback.html: For an A-to-B distance of 120 km, the downstream leg takes 120 / 18 = 6 2/3 hours and the 60 km upstream return takes 60 / 10 = 6 hours, so this distance corresponds to a total journey of 12 2/3 hours.

For an A-to-B distance of 140 km, the downstream leg takes 140 / 18 = 7 7/9 hours and the 70 km upstream return takes 70 / 10 = 7 hours, so this distance corresponds to a total journey of 14 7/9 hours.

For an A-to-B distance of 160 km, the downstream leg takes 160 / 18 = 8 8/9 hours and the 80 km upstream return takes 80 / 10 = 8 hours, so this distance corresponds to a total journey of 16 8/9 hours.
For an A-to-B distance of 180 km, the downstream leg takes 180 / 18 = 10 hours and the 90 km upstream return takes 90 / 10 = 9 hours, so this distance corresponds to a total journey of 19 hours.

title: IOCL Technical Attendant Numerical Ability 2024 Q81
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: एक आदमी स्थिर जल में 9 km/h की चाल से नाव चला सकता है। उसे धारा की दिशा की तुलना में, धारा की विपरीत दिशा में उतनी ही दूरी तय करने में, दोगुना समय लगता है। धारा की चाल (km/h में) ज्ञात कीजिए।
solution:
अवधारणा

यदि स्थिर जल में नाव की चाल u और धारा की चाल v हो, तो अनुप्रवाह चाल u + v तथा प्रतिप्रवाह चाल u − v होती है।

समान दूरी d के लिए समय चाल के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है; अर्थात t = d/s।

प्रयोग

  1. यहाँ u = 9 km/h और धारा की चाल v km/h मानते हैं। इसलिए अनुप्रवाह चाल 9 + v तथा प्रतिप्रवाह चाल 9 − v है।

  2. दूरी d मानने पर प्रतिप्रवाह समय d/(9 − v) और अनुप्रवाह समय d/(9 + v) होगा। प्रश्नानुसार d/(9 − v) = 2d/(9 + v)।

  3. d को निरस्त करने पर 9 + v = 2(9 − v) मिलता है।

  4. अतः 9 + v = 18 − 2v, इसलिए 3v = 9 और v = 3 km/h।

पुनः-जाँच

v = 3 रखने पर अनुप्रवाह चाल 12 km/h और प्रतिप्रवाह चाल 6 km/h होती है। समान दूरी के लिए प्रतिप्रवाह समय का अनुप्रवाह समय से अनुपात 12/6 = 2 है, जो दी गई शर्त की पुष्टि करता है।

इसलिए धारा की चाल 3 km/h है।

धारा की चाल 3 km/h मानने पर अनुप्रवाह और प्रतिप्रवाह चालें क्रमशः 12 तथा 6 km/h होती हैं; समान दूरी के लिए प्रतिप्रवाह-से-अनुप्रवाह समय-अनुपात 12/6 = 2 बनता है।
धारा की चाल 2 km/h मानने पर अनुप्रवाह और प्रतिप्रवाह चालें क्रमशः 11 तथा 7 km/h होती हैं; समान दूरी के लिए प्रतिप्रवाह-से-अनुप्रवाह समय-अनुपात 11/7 बनता है।
धारा की चाल 4 km/h मानने पर अनुप्रवाह और प्रतिप्रवाह चालें क्रमशः 13 तथा 5 km/h होती हैं; समान दूरी के लिए प्रतिप्रवाह-से-अनुप्रवाह समय-अनुपात 13/5 बनता है।

title: Boat takes an hour to cover certain distance downstream in

text: A boat takes an hour to cover a certain distance downstream in a river. It takes 1*1/2 hour to cover the same distance upstream. Assuming that the speed of boat is same in both downstream and upstream directions, what is the ratio of speed of boat to that of stream in the river?
solution:
Let the speed of the boat be B and the stream be S.
Since distance is constant, (B + S) × 1 = (B - S) × 1.5. Expanding gives B + S = 1.5B - 1.5S.
Rearranging terms yields 2.5S = 0.5B, which simplifies to B = 5S.
Thus, the ratio of boat speed to stream speed is 5:1.

title: If man walks km/h, he is late to his office

text: If a man walks 3 km/h, he is late to his office by 20 minutes. If he increases his speed to 6 km/h, he reaches the office 30 minutes early. The distance of his office from the starting place is ______.
solution:
Concept

For a fixed distance, time = distance ÷ speed. When the same distance is covered at two different speeds, the difference between the two travel times equals the total gap between the two arrival outcomes. If one trip is late by L and the other is early by E (relative to the same scheduled time), the slower trip takes (L + E) more time than the faster trip.

Application

Let the distance be d km. The scheduled (on-time) duration is the same in both cases, so we compare the two actual travel times.

  1. At 3 km/h the man is 20 min late and at 6 km/h he is 30 min early, so the slower trip takes 20 + 30 = 50 minutes longer than the faster trip.

  2. Convert the gap to hours: 50 minutes = 50 ÷ 60 = 5/6 hour.

  3. Travel time at 3 km/h is d/3 h; at 6 km/h it is d/6 h. Set their difference equal to the gap: d/3 − d/6 = 5/6.

  4. Combine the left side: d/3 − d/6 = (2d − d)/6 = d/6. So d/6 = 5/6.

  5. Multiply both sides by 6: d = 5. The distance is 5 km.

Cross-check

At 3 km/h, 5 km takes 5/3 h = 1 h 40 min; at 6 km/h, 5 km takes 5/6 h = 50 min. The difference is 1 h 40 min − 50 min = 50 min, matching the 20-min-late-plus-30-min-early gap. Hence 5 km is consistent.

optionFeedback.html: 6 km results from miscounting the combined effect of being late and being early — adding their minutes as if to a full hour rather than the smaller true total. Overstating the time gap leaves the journey times unable to match both stated conditions.

5 km is the distance whose travel times at the two speeds differ by exactly the amount implied by arriving 20 minutes late versus 30 minutes early; the slow and fast journeys line up with both stated outcomes.

A 5.5-km distance makes the two travel times differ by more minutes than the late-and-early conditions allow, so the timing no longer fits both outcomes — a sign the figure was estimated rather than derived from the speed relationship.
4 km results from under-counting how the late time and the early time combine, using too small a minute total. Shrinking the gap this way pulls the distance below its correct value.

text: A candidate secured 36% marks in a class and failed by 24 marks. Another candidate secured 43% marks in the same exam and got 18 extra marks than the passing marks. Find the sum of the maximum marks and the passing marks of that exam ?

Let the total (maximum) marks be y and the passing marks be x.

  2. Second candidate: scored 43% of total and got 18 marks more than passing, so 43/100 × y - 18 = x.

  3. Equate the two expressions for x: 36/100 y + 24 = 43/100 y - 18.

solution:
To compare fractions with different denominators, convert each fraction to its decimal value (divide the numerator by the denominator) or cross-multiply any two fractions being compared — whichever side gives the larger cross-product is the larger fraction. Applying this consistently across a chain shows whether the fractions are truly in ascending (or descending) order.

  1. Convert each fraction in this option to a decimal: 17/27 ≈ 0.6296, 15/22 ≈ 0.6818, and 13/17 ≈ 0.7647.

  2. Compare the decimals in order: 0.6296 < 0.6818, and 0.6818 < 0.7647.

  3. Both comparisons hold, so 17/27 < 15/22 < 13/17 is a genuine ascending chain.

Cross-multiplication confirms the same result without rounding: for 17/27 vs 15/22, 17 × 22 = 374 and 27 × 15 = 405, and since 374 < 405, 17/27 < 15/22. For 15/22 vs 13/17, 15 × 17 = 255 and 22 × 13 = 286, and since 255 < 286, 15/22 < 13/17. Both cross-multiplication checks agree with the decimal comparison, confirming the ascending order is exact, not just a rounding artifact.

Converting each fraction to a decimal gives a strictly increasing run: 17/27 ≈ 0.630, 15/22 ≈ 0.682, and 13/17 ≈ 0.765 — each value is greater than the one before it, so this chain is in true ascending order.

title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q95

text: In a ring, the ratio of gold and silver is 6 : 4. What is the percentage of gold in the ring?
solution:
Concept: When a quantity is split into parts according to a ratio, the percentage share of any part equals (that part's value ÷ sum of all ratio parts) × 100.

Application:

  1. The ratio of gold to silver in the ring is 6 : 4.

  2. The sum of the ratio parts is 6 + 4 = 10.

  3. Gold's share of the ring is 6 parts out of the 10 total parts.

  4. Percentage of gold = (6 ÷ 10) × 100 = 60%.

Cross-check: Silver's percentage = (4 ÷ 10) × 100 = 40%. Since 60% + 40% = 100%, the two shares account for the whole ring, confirming the calculation. Equivalently, 6 : 4 simplifies to 3 : 2, and 3/(3+2) = 3/5 = 60%, the same result by an independent route.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2023 Q66

text: If 20% of A = 30% of B = 1/6 of C, then A : B : C is:
solution:
Concept — when several different multiples of different quantities are all set equal to one another, give that common value a single name, say k. Each quantity is then k divided by its own multiplier, so the quantities come out inversely proportional to those multipliers: the larger the fraction taken of a quantity, the smaller that quantity must be to reach the same k. Percentages and fractions therefore have to be rewritten as plain multiplying factors before the rule can be used.

Application — convert every expression to a multiplier, equate them, then solve for each letter.

  1. Rewrite each expression as a plain multiplier of its own letter: 20% of A = A/5, 30% of B = 3B/10, and one-sixth of C = C/6.

  2. All three are equal, so set them to one common value k: A/5 = 3B/10 = C/6 = k.

  3. Solve each equation for its own letter: A = 5k, B = 10k/3, and C = 6k.

  4. Write the ratio and cancel the common k: A : B : C = 5 : 10/3 : 6.

  5. Multiply every term by 3 to clear the fraction: A : B : C = 15 : 10 : 18.

Cross-check — substitute a value back, and test the inverse-proportion reasoning independently.

  • Take k = 30. Then A = 150, B = 100 and C = 180. Checking: 20% of 150 = 30, 30% of 100 = 30, and 1/6 of 180 = 30, so all three expressions do agree, and 150 : 100 : 180 reduces to 15 : 10 : 18.

  • Inverse-proportion sanity check: the multipliers are 0.30 for B, 0.20 for A and about 0.167 for C; since a larger multiplier needs a smaller quantity to reach the same k, the sizes must run C > A > B, and 18 > 15 > 10 follows that order.

Result — A : B : C = 15 : 10 : 18.

title: What part of is
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: What part of 1/12 is 3/8?
solution:
Concept

The phrase "what part of A is B" asks how many times the reference quantity A fits into B. By definition this part (or fraction) equals B divided by A: part = B / A. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

Application

  1. Identify the reference A = 1/12 (the quantity we measure against) and the target B = 3/8.

  2. Set up the part as a division: part = B / A = (3/8) / (1/12).

  3. Replace division by 1/12 with multiplication by its reciprocal 12/1: part = (3/8) × 12.

  4. Multiply: (3 × 12) / 8 = 36 / 8.

  5. Reduce 36/8 by dividing numerator and denominator by 4: 36/8 = 9/2.

Cross-check

Verify by multiplying the answer back by the reference: (9/2) × (1/12) = 9/24 = 3/8, which is exactly the target B. So 3/8 is 9/2 of 1/12.

1/12 is the reference value already given in the question, not a result of any computation — selecting it directly skips working out the relationship between the two given fractions.

Concept

Only valid votes decide an election. When a fraction of all votes is invalid, Valid votes = Total votes × (1 − invalid fraction). The two candidates together hold all the valid votes: 55% of 6000 = 3300 and 45% of 6000 = 2700, and 3300 + 2700 = 6000, which is exactly the valid-vote count. This confirms 2700.

When a quantity passes through several percentage-based stages in sequence, the value at the end of the chain equals the original amount multiplied by the product of every stage's fraction. title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q72
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: In a university examination, it was found that 42% of the students passed in both English and Mathematics, 64% passed in Mathematics, and 52% passed in English. What is the percentage of students who failed in both the subjects?
solution:
For two overlapping groups expressed as percentages of the same population, the percentage belonging to at least one of the two groups equals the sum of the two individual percentages minus the percentage common to both groups, since the common portion would otherwise be counted twice. The percentage belonging to neither group then equals 100% minus this combined figure.

  1. Let M = percentage of students who passed in Mathematics = 64%, E = percentage of students who passed in English = 52%, and B = percentage of students who passed in both subjects = 42%.

  2. The percentage of students who passed in at least one of the two subjects = M + E − B = 64% + 52% − 42% = 74%.

  3. The percentage of students who failed in both subjects is the complement of this figure with respect to the whole student population: 100% − 74% = 26%.

As an independent check, partition the students into three mutually exclusive groups: those passing English only (52% − 42% = 10%), those passing Mathematics only (64% − 42% = 22%), and those passing both subjects (42%). These three groups add up to 10% + 22% + 42% = 74% of students passing at least one subject, matching the figure obtained above and confirming that 26% of the students failed in both subjects.

solution:
अवधारणा

प्रतिशत परिवर्तन निकालने के लिए पहले मूल मात्रा और परिवर्तित मात्रा को समान आधार पर व्यक्त किया जाता है। आय = बचत + व्यय संबंध हर अवस्था में लागू रहता है।

यदि किसी मात्रा का नया मान पुराने मान का (1 + r/100) गुना हो, तो प्रतिशत वृद्धि = (वृद्धि ÷ पुराना मान) × 100 होती है।

अनुप्रयोग

  1. पुरानी मासिक आय को 100 इकाई मानें।

  2. पुरानी बचत = 20% × 100 = 20 इकाई, इसलिए पुराना व्यय = 100 − 20 = 80 इकाई।

  3. आय में 30% वृद्धि के बाद नई आय = 100 × 1.30 = 130 इकाई।

  4. बचत पिछली बचत से 20% अधिक है, इसलिए नई बचत = 20 × 1.20 = 24 इकाई।

  5. नया व्यय = नई आय − नई बचत = 130 − 24 = 106 इकाई। अतः व्यय में वृद्धि = 106 − 80 = 26 इकाई।

  6. व्यय में प्रतिशत वृद्धि = (26 ÷ 80) × 100 = 32.5%।

पुनः-जाँच

  1. पुराने व्यय को 32.5% बढ़ाने पर 80 × 1.325 = 106 इकाई मिलता है।

  2. नई आय में से यह व्यय घटाने पर 130 − 106 = 24 इकाई बचती है, जो पुरानी 20 इकाई बचत से 20% अधिक है।

इसलिए व्यय में प्रतिशत वृद्धि 32.5% है।

title: The population of town increases by in the first year

text: The population of a town increases by 80% in the first year and further it increases by 20% in the second year. The overall increase percentage in population in two years is
solution:
To find the overall percentage increase when a population grows sequentially, you cannot simply add the percentages. Instead, you must calculate the effect of each increase on the new total.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Assume an initial value: Let the initial population be 100.

First-year increase (80%):

Increase = 80% of 100 = 80.

New population = 100 + 80 = 180.

Second-year increase (20%):

Increase = 20% of the new population (180).

Calculation: 0.20 × 180 = 36.

New population = 180 + 36 = 216.

Calculate overall percentage increase:

Total increase = Final population - Initial population = 216 - 100 = 116.

Percentage increase = (Total increase / Initial population) × 100

(116 / 100) × 100 = 116%.

title: The price of sugar has increased by Find the percentage

text: The price of sugar has increased by 25%. Find the percentage reduction in consumption so as to not increase the expenditure?
solution:
Key idea: keep expenditure constant when price changes.

  • Let the original price be P and original consumption be Q. Original expenditure = P × Q.

  • After a 25% price increase, new price = 1.25 × P. Let new consumption be Q'. To keep expenditure the same: 1.25P × Q' = P × Q.

  • Solve for Q': Q' = Q / 1.25 = 0.8 Q. Thus consumption must be 80% of the original.

  • Reduction = (Q − Q')/Q = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2 = 20%.

Answer: 20% reduction in consumption.

text: An instrument cost a certain factory Rs. 520,000. If it depreciates in value by 16.5% the first year, 15% the next year, 13.5% the third year, and so on, what will be its value (in Rs.) at the end of 8 years, all percentages applying to the original cost?
solution:
CONCEPT: When each depreciation rate is applied to the original cost, the losses add directly as percentages of that original cost.

For rates that form an arithmetic sequence, use the arithmetic-series sum to get the total depreciation percentage, then subtract that percentage from 100% to find the remaining value.

  3. So the total depreciation is 90% of Rs. 520,000 = Rs. 468,000.

  4. The value left is Rs. 520,000 - Rs. 468,000 = Rs. 52,000.

CROSS-CHECK: If 90% of the original cost is depreciated, 10% remains; 10% of Rs. 520,000 is Rs. 52,000.

Result: the value at the end of 8 years is Rs. 52,000.

text: In a school number of students increases in each year by 10%. If in the first year number of students is 500, what will be the number of students in the third year?
solution:
Concept: In successive percentage change, when a quantity grows by the same rate r% at the end of every period, each period's increase is calculated on that period's already-grown total, not on the original amount again. After n periods the amount equals the original amount multiplied by (1 + r/100), applied once per period.

Application:

  1. Year 1 count = 500 (given).

  2. Apply the first year's 10% increase to get Year 2: 500 × 1.10 = 550.

  3. Apply the second year's 10% increase to Year 2's total to get Year 3: 550 × 1.10 = 605.

Cross-check: Two successive 10% increases multiply the original amount by 1.10 × 1.10 = 1.21, so 500 × 1.21 = 605 — matching the step-by-step result. (Simply adding 10% + 10% = 20% of the original 500 directly would ignore that the second increase applies to the grown total, giving the wrong figure of 600.)

So the number of students in the third year is 605.

title: DSSSB TGT English 24 Aug 2025 Shift 1 Q48
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
subtopic: Percentage in Population / Growth / Successive Years
text: The present population of a village is 8,820. Twenty years ago, it was 8,000. Assuming the population increases at a constant rate every 10 years, find the percentage rate of increase per 10 years.
solution:
When a quantity grows at a constant percentage rate every fixed time period, its value after n such periods follows the compound-growth relation: Final value = Initial value × (1 + r)n, where r is the growth rate per period as a decimal — the same relation used for compound interest.

  1. The population 20 years before the present (two 10-year periods earlier) was 8,000, and the present population is 8,820, so the number of growth periods is n = 20 ÷ 10 = 2.

  2. Apply the compound-growth relation with n = 2: 8,000 × (1 + r)2 = 8,820.

  3. Divide both sides by 8,000: (1 + r)2 = 8,820 ÷ 8,000 = 1.1025.

  4. Take the square root of both sides: 1 + r = √1.1025 = 1.05.

  5. Subtract 1 from both sides: r = 0.05, i.e., the rate of increase is 5% per 10-year period.

Cross-check: starting from 8,000 and applying a 5% increase twice — 8,000 × 1.05 = 8,400 after the first 10 years, then 8,400 × 1.05 = 8,820 after the second 10 years — reproduces the given present population exactly, confirming the computed rate.

So the population increases at 5% per 10-year period.

If the population grew at 6% every 10 years starting from a base of 8,000, the population at the 10-year mark would be 8,000 × 1.06 = 8,480.
If the population grew at 8% every 10 years starting from a base of 8,000, the population at the 10-year mark would be 8,000 × 1.08 = 8,640.
If the population grew at 5% every 10 years starting from a base of 8,000, the population at the 10-year mark would be 8,000 × 1.05 = 8,400.

text: A person multiplied a number by 15/11 instead of 11/15. What is the percentage error in calculation?
solution:
Step-by-Step Solution

  1. Define the Number: Let the number be x.

  2. Determine the Values:

    • Correct value = (11/15) * x

    • Incorrect value = (15/11) * x

  3. Calculate the Absolute Error: The error is the difference between the incorrect value and the correct value.

    • Error = (15/11)x - (11/15)x

    • To subtract, find a common denominator (11 * 15 = 165).

    • Error = (225x / 165) - (121x / 165) = (104/165)x.

  4. Calculate Percentage Error: The formula for percentage error is (Error / Correct Value) * 100.

    • Percentage Error = [((104/165)x) / ((11/15)x)] * 100

    • Percentage Error = (104 / 165) * (15 / 11) * 100

    • Simplify: 104 / 11 * 1/11 * 100 (since 165/15 = 11)

    • Percentage Error = (104 / 121) * 100 = 10400 / 121%.

  5. Convert to Mixed Fraction:

    • 10400 divided by 121 equals 85 with a remainder of 115.

    • Thus, the result is 85 and 115/121%.

title: Diagonally opposite vertex in an axis-aligned unit cube
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A cube of side 1 unit is placed so that the origin coincides with one of its top vertices and the three coordinate axes lie along three edges of the cube. What are the coordinates of the vertex diagonally opposite to the vertex whose coordinates are (1, 0, 1)?
solution:
Concept

For an axis-aligned unit cube, the three coordinate axes run along the three cube edges that meet at the origin, so the cube occupies the region where every coordinate lies between 0 and 1 and each vertex has coordinates that are each either 0 or 1. Two vertices lie at opposite ends of the cube's space (body) diagonal exactly when each coordinate of one is the complement of the other: every 0 becomes 1 and every 1 becomes 0. Such a pair is separated by the longest distance inside the cube, the space diagonal of length √3.

Here the origin is the vertex where the three positive axis directions start, taken along the cube's edges. Calling it a "top" vertex only names its position along one axis; it does not move the cube into negative coordinates and does not change the complement rule used to find the diagonally opposite vertex. So all eight vertices still have 0/1 coordinates, and the answer is found the same way whichever vertex you label "top" or "bottom".

Applying it here

  1. Write the coordinates of the given vertex: (1, 0, 1).

  2. Complement each coordinate independently: 1 → 0, 0 → 1, 1 → 0.

  3. Read off the resulting vertex: (0, 1, 0).

Cross-check

Measure the straight-line distance from (1, 0, 1) to (0, 1, 0): √((1−0)2 + (0−1)2 + (1−0)2) = √3. That equals the cube's full space diagonal, so these two vertices are joined by the longest diagonal of the cube. For comparison, (0, 0, 0) lies only √2 away (a face diagonal) and (1, 1, 1) lies only 1 unit away (an edge), so the diagonal-opposite of (1, 0, 1) is the vertex (0, 1, 0).

optionFeedback.html: (0, 0, 0) is the origin vertex; it lies only a face diagonal (√2) away from (1, 0, 1) and shares one coordinate axis with it, so it is not at the far end of the cube's space diagonal from (1, 0, 1).
(0, -1, 0) uses a negative coordinate, but every vertex of this unit cube has each coordinate equal to 0 or 1, so this point is not a vertex of the cube at all.
(0, 1, 0) is the coordinate-by-coordinate complement of (1, 0, 1) and lies √3 from it, the full length of the cube's space diagonal.
(1, 1, 1) is the complement of the origin (0, 0, 0), so it pairs diagonally with (0, 0, 0); from (1, 0, 1) it is only one edge (1 unit) away.

title: Set contains points whose abscissa and ordinate are both natural
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Set S contains points whose abscissa and ordinate are both natural numbers. Point P, an element in set S has the property that the sum of the distances from point P to the point (3,0) and the point (0,5) is the lowest among all elements in set S. What is the sum of abscissa and ordinate of point P?
solution:
Key idea: The sum of distances to two fixed points is minimized (without restrictions) by any point on the segment joining those two points. Here we must choose a point with integer positive coordinates, so we test lattice points near that segment.

The two fixed points are (3,0) and (0,5). The line through them has equation x/3 + y/5 = 1, i.e. 5x + 3y = 15. Natural numbers are taken here as positive integers (1,2,...).

Check integer points close to the line. The closest small positive integer points to the segment are (1,2), (1,3), (2,1), and (2,2). Compute the total distances to (3,0) and (0,5):

  • Point (1,2): distance to (3,0) = sqrt8, distance to (0,5) = sqrt10, total = sqrt8 + sqrt10 ≈ 5.99

  • Point (1,3): distance to (3,0) = sqrt13, distance to (0,5) = sqrt5, total = sqrt13 + sqrt5 ≈ 5.842

  • Point (2,1): distance to (3,0) = sqrt2, distance to (0,5) = sqrt20, total = sqrt2 + sqrt20 ≈ 5.886

  • Point (2,2): distance to (3,0) = sqrt5, distance to (0,5) = sqrt13, total = sqrt5 + sqrt13 ≈ 5.842

Conclusion: The smallest total distance among these lattice points is sqrt13 + sqrt5, achieved by both (1,3) and (2,2). Both have abscissa + ordinate = 4, so the required sum is 4.

Answer: 4

Incorrect. A coordinate-sum of 3 corresponds to points (1,2) or (2,1). Their total distances are sqrt8 + sqrt10 ≈ 5.99 and sqrt2 + sqrt20 ≈ 5.886 respectively, both larger than the minimum sqrt13 + sqrt5 ≈ 5.842, so sum 3 is not minimal.

Correct. The lattice points (1,3) and (2,2) both give the minimal total distance equal to sqrt13 + sqrt5 ≈ 5.842, so the sum of abscissa and ordinate of point P is 4.

title: In the figure BD DC and ∠DBC What is the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: In the figure BD = DC and ∠DBC = 25°. What is the value of ∠BAC?
solution:
Concept

Two inscribed angles that stand on the same chord from opposite arcs of a circle are supplementary (they add to 180°). Also, in a triangle the angles opposite two equal sides are themselves equal (isosceles base angles).

Application

  1. In triangle BDC the sides BD and DC are equal, so the base angles opposite them are equal: ∠DCB = ∠DBC = 25°.

  2. The angles of triangle BDC sum to 180°, so ∠BDC = 180° − 25° − 25° = 130°.

  3. ∠BAC and ∠BDC both stand on the same chord BC, but A lies on the major arc and D on the minor arc, i.e. on opposite arcs. Such inscribed angles are supplementary: ∠BAC + ∠BDC = 180°.

  4. Therefore ∠BAC = 180° − 130° = 50°.

Cross-check

Independent check: the equal chords BD and DC cut off equal arcs, each of arc-measure 2 × 25° = 50° (the inscribed angle is half its arc). Arc BDC (from B to C through D) = 50° + 50° = 100°, so the remaining arc BAC (from B to C through A) = 360° − 100° = 260°. The inscribed angle ∠BDC on arc BAC equals half of it (130°), and ∠BAC on arc BDC equals 100° ÷ 2 = 50°, confirming ∠BAC = 50°.

optionFeedback.html: 30° does not come from any valid step in this configuration. It typically appears when the marked 25° is treated as if it sits in a simple proportion with the unknown angle, but 25° is a base angle of the isosceles triangle BDC and must be carried through that triangle and the inscribed-angle relation, not scaled by an invented factor.

100° is the combined arc that the two equal chords BD and DC subtend, not the angle formed at the vertex A. Stopping at this arc total and reporting it as ∠BAC confuses an arc on the circle with the angle the question actually asks for.
With BD = DC the base angles give ∠DCB = ∠DBC = 25°, so ∠BDC = 130°. Since A and D lie on opposite arcs of chord BC, ∠BAC = 180° − 130° = 50°.

90° assumes ∠BAC is an angle in a semicircle, i.e. that BC is a diameter. Nothing in the data makes BC a diameter; BC is just the chord subtended from both A and D, so the semicircle (Thales) rule does not apply here.

Solve for k:

k - 2 = 6 or k - 2 = -6
k = 8 or k = -4

Since the problem states k > 0, we take k = 8.

Calculate k² + 6:
(8)² + 6 = 64 + 6 = 70

title: In rectangle grid shown below, each cell is rectangle. How

title: The length of rectangular plot is meters more than its
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: The length of a rectangular plot is 20 meters more than its breadth. If the cost of fencing the plot @ ₹26.50 per meter is ₹5300, what is the length of the plot in meters?
solution:
Let breadth = x meters. Then length = x + 20 meters.

Step 1: Convert the total fencing cost to perimeter.

Perimeter = total cost ÷ cost per meter = 5300 ÷ 26.5 = 200 meters.

Step 2: Use the rectangle perimeter formula and solve for x.

  1. Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 2[(x + 20) + x] = 200.

  2. Divide both sides by 2: (x + 20) + x = 100 ⇒ 2x + 20 = 100.

  3. Solve: 2x = 80 ⇒ x = 40.

  4. Length = x + 20 = 40 + 20 = 60 meters.

title: Circular wire of radius cm is cut and bent in

text: A circular wire of radius 28 cm is cut and bent in the form of a rectangle whose sides are in the ratio 6:5. Then the smaller side of the rectangle :
solution:
Concept: When a wire is cut and re-bent into another closed shape, its total length is conserved — the circle's circumference before bending equals the rectangle's perimeter after bending, so 2πr = 2(l + w).

  1. Circumference of the circle = 2πr = 2 × (22/7) × 28 = 176 cm — this is the fixed length of the wire.

  2. This 176 cm becomes the rectangle's perimeter, so 2(l + w) = 176, i.e., l + w = 88 cm.

  3. The sides are in the ratio 6 : 5, so let the sides be 6x and 5x.

  4. 6x + 5x = 88, so 11x = 88, so x = 8.

  5. So the two sides are 6 × 8 = 48 cm and 5 × 8 = 40 cm; the smaller side is 40 cm.

Cross-check: Perimeter = 2 × (48 + 40) = 2 × 88 = 176 cm, which matches the circle's circumference — confirming the split is correct.

Concept

A pathway of uniform width laid across a rectangle, parallel to one side, is itself a rectangle. Its area equals its width multiplied by the side it spans. So for a strip parallel to the breadth, Area = width × breadth. Combined with a stated relation between length and breadth, this fixes both dimensions.

  2. A pathway of width 4 m runs parallel to the breadth, so it spans the full breadth b. Its area = 4 × b.

  3. Set this equal to the given area: 4 × b = 352.

  4. Solve for the breadth: b = 352 ÷ 4 = 88 m.

  5. Length = 2b = 2 × 88 = 176 m.

Cross-check

With breadth 88 m, a 4 m strip across it covers 4 × 88 = 352 m2, matching the given pathway area, and the length 176 m is exactly twice 88 m. Both conditions hold, so the length is 176 m.

title: If three sides of the triangle are given as cm,
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: If three sides of the triangle are given as 32 cm, 34 cm and 34 cm, then the area of the triangle is:
solution:
Concept

For a triangle with all three sides known, the area equals one-half times the base times the corresponding height. When two sides are equal (isosceles), the perpendicular dropped from the apex to the unequal side bisects that side, so its height can be found by the Pythagoras theorem: (slant side)² = (half-base)² + (height)².

Application

  1. The sides are 32 cm, 34 cm and 34 cm. Two sides are equal (34 = 34), so the triangle is isosceles with base 32 cm and equal sides 34 cm.

  2. Drop a perpendicular from the apex to the 32 cm base; it bisects the base into two parts of 16 cm each.

  3. Apply Pythagoras in one right half: height² = 34² − 16² = 1156 − 256 = 900, so height = 30 cm.

  4. Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 32 × 30 = 16 × 30 = 480 cm².

Cross-check

Heron's formula gives the same result independently. Semi-perimeter s = (32 + 34 + 34) ÷ 2 = 50. Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)) = √(50 × 18 × 16 × 16) = √230400 = 480 cm². Both methods agree, confirming the area is 480 cm².

title: Ravi cuts square field of maximum possible area from his

Remaining area = Area of circle - Area of square.

title: The altitude drawn to the base of an isosceles triangle
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: The altitude drawn to the base of an isosceles triangle is 12 cm and the perimeter is 36 cm. Find the area (in cm2) of the triangle.
solution:
Concept: In an isosceles triangle, the altitude drawn to the base bisects that base and splits the triangle into two congruent right triangles. In each of them the legs are the altitude and half the base, and the hypotenuse is one of the two equal sides. Two relations therefore govern every such triangle: the Pythagorean relation (equal side)2 = (half of base)2 + (altitude)2, and the area formula Area = 1/2 × base × altitude.

Application: Let each equal side be a cm and the base be b cm, with the altitude to the base equal to 12 cm.

  1. Perimeter: 2a + b = 36, so a = 18 − b/2.

  2. The altitude bisects the base, so one right triangle has legs b/2 and 12 with hypotenuse a: a2 = (b/2)2 + 122.

  3. Substitute a = 18 − b/2: (18 − b/2)2 = (b/2)2 + 144.

  4. Expand the left-hand side: 324 − 18b + b2/4 = b2/4 + 144.

  5. The b2/4 terms cancel, leaving 324 − 18b = 144, so 18b = 180 and b = 10.

  6. Then a = 18 − 10/2 = 13, so the base is 10 cm and each equal side is 13 cm.

  7. Area = 1/2 × base × altitude = 1/2 × 10 × 12 = 60 cm2.

Cross-check: the right triangle formed by the altitude has legs 5 cm and 12 cm and hypotenuse 13 cm, the 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple, and the three sides give a perimeter of 13 + 13 + 10 = 36 cm, exactly the value stated in the question.

Hence the area of the triangle is 60 cm2.

title: If three sides of the triangle is given cm, cm
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: If three sides of the triangle is given 18 cm, 41 cm and 41 cm. Then the area of triangle is:
solution:
Concept

For a triangle whose three side lengths are known, the area is given by Heron's formula. If the sides are a, b, c and the semi-perimeter is s = (a + b + c)/2, then Area = √[ s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c) ]. For an isosceles triangle (two equal sides) the same result also follows from Area = ½ × base × height, where the height drops from the apex to the midpoint of the unequal base.

Application

  1. Identify the sides: a = 18, b = 41, c = 41. The two equal sides are 41, so the base is 18.

  2. Semi-perimeter: s = (18 + 41 + 41) / 2 = 100 / 2 = 50.

  3. Substitute into Heron's formula: Area = √[ 50 × (50 − 18) × (50 − 41) × (50 − 41) ] = √[ 50 × 32 × 9 × 9 ].

  4. Simplify under the root: 50 × 32 = 1600, and 9 × 9 = 81, so Area = √(1600 × 81) = √1600 × √81 = 40 × 9 = 360.

Therefore the area is 360 cm2.

Cross-check

Using the height method: the base 18 is split into two halves of 9. The height h satisfies h = √(41² − 9²) = √(1681 − 81) = √1600 = 40. Then Area = ½ × 18 × 40 = 360 cm2, which agrees with Heron's formula.

text: The diagonal of a rectangle is 17 cm long and its perimeter is 46 cm. The area of the rectangle is:
solution:

In a rectangle of length l and breadth b, three measurements are linked: the perimeter is 2(l + b), the diagonal d satisfies the Pythagoras relation l2 + b2 = d2, and the area is l × b.

The identity (l + b)2 = l2 + b2 + 2lb joins all three, so the product lb - the area - follows from the perimeter and the diagonal alone, without ever finding l and b separately.

text: The breadth of a rectangular hall is 5/8 of its length. If the area of the floor is 160 metre2, then what is the difference between the length and breadth of the hall?
solution:
Concept:

For a rectangle, Area = Length x Breadth. When the breadth is given as a fixed fraction of the length (B = k x L for some constant k), substituting into the area formula gives a single-variable equation in L: Area = k x L2, which can be solved for L, then for B, then for any combination of the two such as their difference.

Applying it here:

  1. Let the length of the hall be L. Since the breadth is 5/8 of the length, B = (5/8)L.

  2. Using Area = Length x Breadth: 160 = L x (5/8)L = (5/8)L2.

  3. Rearranging gives L2 = 160 x (8/5) = 256, so L = 16 metres.

  4. Finding the breadth: B = (5/8) x 16 = 10 metres.

  5. Computing the difference: L - B = 16 - 10 = 6 metres.

Cross-check:

With L = 16 m and B = 10 m: the ratio B/L = 10/16 = 5/8 matches the given breadth-to-length ratio, and the area L x B = 16 x 10 = 160 square metres matches the given floor area, so both conditions in the problem are satisfied.

The difference between the length and the breadth of the hall is 6 metres.

text: A solid cube made of steel is melted and recast such that its length, breadth and height changes as +10%, +10%, -20%. What is the percentage change in surface area of this cube?

Let the original cube have side length s. The original surface area is 6s².

After recasting, the new dimensions are: length = 1.1s (+10%), breadth = 1.1s (+10%), height = 0.8s (−20%).

Surface area of the resulting cuboid = 2(ab + bc + ac) = 2·s²·(1.1·1.1 + 1.1·0.8 + 1.1·0.8).

Compute inside the parentheses: 1.1·1.1 = 1.21 and 1.1·0.8 = 0.88, so the sum is 1.21 + 0.88 + 0.88 = 2.97. Thus the new surface area = 2·s²·2.97 = 5.94·s².

Percentage change = (new − original)/original × 100% = (5.94·s² − 6·s²)/(6·s²) × 100% = (−0.06/6) × 100% = −1%.

Answer: -1% (the surface area decreases by 1%).

There is a rectangular path just inside a rectangular park. Width of the path is 2 cm. If length of park is decreased by 4 cm then, it becomes a square. Area of the rectangle is 1⅓ times the area of the path.
From the above given information which of the following can be found out.
(i) Area of path
(ii) Length of the park
(iii) Sum of perimeter of the rectangular park and perimeter of the path (both external and internal perimeter)
solution:
Let the park breadth be x cm and length be x + 4 cm. Since the path is 2 cm wide inside the park, the inner rectangle is (x - 4) by x.

The path area is x(x + 4) - x(x - 4) = 8x. Given park area is 1 1/3 times the path area, x(x + 4) = (4/3) x 8x.

This determines the park dimensions, so the path area, length of the park, and required perimeters can all be found.

title: The curved surface area of hemisphere is cm², then its
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: The curved surface area of a hemisphere is 8π cm², then its radius is:
solution:
Concept

The curved (lateral) surface of a hemisphere is exactly half of a full sphere's surface. A full sphere has surface area 4πr2; therefore the curved surface area of a hemisphere is CSA = 2πr2. This is the only quantity asked here, so the flat circular base is not counted.

Application

  1. Write the formula: CSA = 2πr2.

  2. Set it equal to the given value: 2πr2 = 8π.

  3. Divide both sides by 2π to isolate r2: r2 = 4.

  4. Take the positive square root (a length is non-negative): r = 2 cm.

Cross-check

Substitute r = 2 back into the formula: 2π(2)2 = 2π × 4 = 8π cm2, which matches the given curved surface area, confirming r = 2 cm.

A non-integer radius like 2.5 cm often comes from mishandling the factor 2π; it does not produce the 8π cm2 stated.
A radius of 2 cm is the value whose curved surface equals the 8π cm2 stated, so it meets the given condition.

title: What is the surface area of sphere with radius of
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: What is the surface area of a sphere with a radius of 14√5 cm (use π = 22/7)?
solution:
Concept: The surface area of a sphere is fixed by its radius alone, through the identity S = 4πr2. The radius enters only as a square, so a radius written as a surd is squared exactly using (a√b)2 = a2b, and no decimal approximation of the surd is needed at any stage.

Application: here the radius is 14√5 cm and the question fixes π = 22/7.

  1. Square the radius exactly: r2 = (14√5)2 = 142 × 5 = 196 × 5 = 980 cm2.

  2. Substitute into the identity: S = 4 × (22/7) × 980 cm2.

  3. Cancel the 7 against 980 before multiplying: 980 ÷ 7 = 140, which leaves S = 4 × 22 × 140.

  4. Multiply the remaining factors: 4 × 22 = 88, and 88 × 140 = 12320.

  5. Therefore S = 12320 cm2.

Cross-check: reverse the arithmetic. 12320 ÷ 4 = 3080, and 3080 × 7/22 = 980, which is exactly r2; since √980 = √(196 × 5) = 14√5, the radius recovered is the one the question gave, so the value is consistent.

Contrast: the factor in front of πr2 decides which figure is being measured — 2πr2 is the curved surface of a hemisphere (6160 cm2 here) and 3πr2 is the total surface of a hemisphere (9240 cm2 here). A full sphere always carries the factor 4.

For a cube of edge length a, two formulas matter: the total surface area is S = 6a2 (six identical square faces), and the space diagonal (corner to opposite corner) is d = a√3. So the diagonal is found by first recovering the edge from the surface area, then scaling that edge by √3.

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q84
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: The internal surface area (in m2) of an open cuboidal tank whose internal length, internal breadth, and internal height are given as 15 m, 17 m, and 16 m, respectively, is:
solution:
Concept

For an open cuboid, the top face is absent, so its internal surface area is the base plus the four side walls.

Thus, for length l, breadth b, and height h, the area is lb + 2lh + 2bh = lb + 2h(l + b).

Application

  1. Base area = 15 × 17 = 255 m2

  2. Area of the two walls along the length = 2 × 15 × 16 = 480 m2

  3. Area of the two walls along the breadth = 2 × 17 × 16 = 544 m2

  4. Total internal surface area = 255 + 480 + 544 = 1279 m2

Cross-check

Using the compact formula: 15 × 17 + 2 × 16 × (15 + 17) = 255 + 1024 = 1279 m2

Therefore, the internal surface area is 1279 m2.

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q85
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: If each side of the cube is increased by 20%, then by what percentage is the surface area increased?
solution:
Concept

When every length of a solid is multiplied by a scale factor k, every area is multiplied by k2. Surface area therefore changes with the square of the linear scale factor.

A percentage increase of r% in a length gives the scale factor 1 + r/100.

Application

  1. Let the original cube side be a. Its surface area is 6a2.

  2. After a 20% increase, the new side is 1.20a.

  3. The new surface area is 6(1.20a)2 = 6 × 1.44a2 = 1.44 times the original surface area.

  4. Hence the fractional increase is 1.44 − 1 = 0.44, which is 44%.

Cross-check

Using percentage points, the area increase is 2 × 20 + 202/100 = 40 + 4 = 44%, confirming the result.

title: DSSSB TGT English 24 Aug 2025 5-7 PM Q55
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A conical tent has to accommodate 75 persons. Each person must have 10 m2 of space on the ground and 95 m3 of air to breathe. Find the approximate height (in m) of the tent.
solution:
Concept

For any cone, Volume = (1/3) x base area x height. Because both the total base area and the total volume are already known as combined totals for all persons, the height can be found directly from this relation without separately finding the radius or using pi.

Application

  1. Total ground (base) area required = 75 persons x 10 sq m per person = 750 sq m. This is the base area of the conical tent.

  2. Total air volume required = 75 persons x 95 cubic m per person = 7125 cubic m. This is the volume of the cone.

  3. Apply the cone volume formula: Volume = (1/3) x base area x height, so 7125 = (1/3) x 750 x height.

  4. Solve for height: height = (3 x 7125) / 750 = 21375 / 750 = 28.5 m.

Cross-check

If the tent were shaped like a cylinder with the same base area, its height would simply be volume / base area = 7125 / 750 = 9.5 m. A cone's volume is exactly one-third of a cylinder sharing the same base and height, so the cone's actual height must be three times this cylinder-equivalent value: 3 x 9.5 m = 28.5 m, confirming the result.

The height of the tent is approximately 28.5 m.

Each of the following problems consist of a question followed by two statements, I and II. You must determine whether the information given by the statements is sufficient to answer the question asked. In addition to the information provided in the statements, you should rely on your knowledge of mathematics and ordinary facts (such as the number of seconds in a minute).

What is the volume of a right circular cylinder?

I. The area of the base of the figure is 196.

II. The height of the figure is 16.

options.html: if the question can be answered by using only statement I
if the question can be answered by using only statement II.

if the question cannot be answered even by using both statements together.

solution:
Answer: The question can be answered using both statements together (the area of the base and the height).

Key idea: Volume of a right circular cylinder = (area of the base) × (height).

  • Statement II provides the height = 16.

Using both pieces of information: volume = 196 × 16 = 3136 (in cubic units).

Conclusion: Neither the base area alone nor the height alone is sufficient, but together they are sufficient to compute the volume.

title: Rectangular Sandbox is wide and long. How many Cubic Metres
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A Rectangular Sandbox is 5 m wide and 2 m long. How many Cubic Metres of Sand is needed to fill the Box into a Depth of 10 cm?
solution:
Solution

To find the volume of sand needed, we calculate the volume of the rectangular sandbox.

Step 1: Identify the dimensions.

Width = 5 m

Length = 2 m

Depth = 10 cm

Step 2: Convert units to be consistent.

Since the required answer is in cubic meters, convert the depth from centimeters to meters.

10 cm = 10 / 100 m = 0.1 m

Step 3: Calculate the volume.

Volume = Width × Length × Depth

Volume = 5 m × 2 m × 0.1 m

Volume = 10 × 0.1 = 1 cubic meter

Therefore, 1 cubic meter of sand is needed.

हिन्दी उत्तर

रेत की आवश्यक मात्रा ज्ञात करने के लिए, हम आयताकार सैंडबॉक्स का आयतन ज्ञात करते हैं।

चरण 1: मापों की पहचान करें।

चौड़ाई = 5 मीटर

लंबाई = 2 मीटर

गहराई = 10 सेमी

चरण 2: इकाइयों को सुसंगत बनाने के लिए रूपांतरित करें।

चूंकि आवश्यक उत्तर घन मीटर में है, सेमी से मीटर में गहराई का रूपांतरण करें।

10 सेमी = 10 / 100 मीटर = 0.1 मीटर

चरण 3: आयतन की गणना करें।

आयतन = चौड़ाई × लंबाई × गहराई

आयतन = 5 मीटर × 2 मीटर × 0.1 मीटर

आयतन = 10 × 0.1 = 1 घन मीटर

अतः, 1 घन मीटर रेत की आवश्यकता होगी।

title: In the given Venn diagram, the 'rectangle' represents 'persons in
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: In a bar survey, the rectangle represents everyone in the bar. The circle represents people who like apple juice, the triangle represents people who like orange juice, and the pentagon represents people who like pineapple juice. The disjoint region counts are: apple only = 15, apple and orange = 8, orange only = 9, orange and pineapple = 6, pineapple only = 18, and rectangle-only (inside the bar but outside all three juice shapes) = 42. How many people in the bar like neither apple juice nor orange juice?
solution:
CONCEPT

For two sets A and B inside a universal set U, “neither A nor B” means the complement U \ (A ∪ B). Every disjoint region outside both A and B is counted, even when it belongs to a third set.

APPLICATION

  1. Take the rectangle as the universal set and exclude every region that lies in the apple circle or the orange triangle.

  2. The remaining disjoint regions are pineapple only, containing 18 people, and rectangle-only, containing 42 people.

  3. Add the remaining region counts: 18 + 42 = 60.

CROSS-CHECK

  1. All six disjoint regions contain 15 + 8 + 9 + 6 + 18 + 42 = 98 people.

  2. The apple-or-orange union contains 15 + 8 + 9 + 6 = 38 people.

  3. Its complement therefore contains 98 − 38 = 60 people.

RESULT

Therefore, 60 people like neither apple juice nor orange juice.

text: Based on the following information, answer the question given below: A businessman has five articles P, Q, R, S and T. I. P weighs double that of Q. II. Q weighs four and half times of R. III. R weighs half that of T. IV. T weighs less than P but more than R. V. S is heavier only than R. Which one of the following is the lightest?
solution:
When several quantities are linked through a chain of ratio statements (double, half, four and a half times, etc.), express every quantity in terms of a single common variable and then compare the resulting numeric coefficients directly -- this avoids working with fractions or reciprocal relations.

  1. Let R = x.

  2. R weighs half that of T, so T = 2R = 2x.

  3. Q weighs four and a half times R, so Q = 4.5R = 4.5x.

  4. P weighs double Q, so P = 2Q = 2(4.5x) = 9x.

  5. S is heavier only than R, so S lies strictly between R and every other article: R < S < T = 2x.

  6. Putting every article on the same scale gives R = x, S with x < S < 2x, T = 2x, Q = 4.5x, and P = 9x, so the ascending order of weight is R < S < T < Q < P.

Checking statement IV independently: T must be less than P and more than R. With T = 2x, P = 9x, R = x, indeed x < 2x < 9x, so the relation holds. S being heavier only than R is also consistent with R < S < T. R is therefore the lightest article.

On the common scale, P works out to 9x -- built from Q, which is itself built from R.
On the common scale, R is the base unit x, the smallest of the five expressed coefficients once S, T, Q and P are placed alongside it.
On the common scale, Q works out to 4.5x -- a value derived directly from its relation to R alone, without folding in P or T.
This choice means the question was left unattempted. Re-read each of the five statements and note how they relate each article to the others before selecting an answer.

title: Thomas bought number of sports goods for Rs If each
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Thomas bought X number of sports goods for Rs 9600. If each item was cheaper by Rs 20 then with the same amount he could have bought 40 more items than X. Find the number of items bought by Thomas ?
solution:
Solution:

  1. Let X be the number of items bought. Then the price per item is 9600/X.

  2. If each item were cheaper by 20, the new price is 9600/X - 20, and with the same Rs 9600 you would buy X + 40 items. Set up the equation: 9600/X - 20 = 9600/(X + 40).

  3. Multiply both sides by X(X + 40) and simplify to get the quadratic equation: X^2 + 40X - 19200 = 0.

  4. Solve the quadratic. Discriminant = 40^2 - 4(1)(-19200) = 78400, sqrt = 280. Thus X = (-40 ± 280)/2, giving X = 120 or X = -160. Discard the negative root.

  5. Therefore the number of items bought is 120.

Answer: 120 items.

If each item were cheaper by 20, the new price is 9600/X - 20 and with the same Rs 9600 you would buy X + 40 items, so set up 9600/X - 20 = 9600/(X + 40). Solving this gives the positive solution X = 120. Thus Thomas bought 120 items.

Incorrect. If you test 160 items, price per item = 9600/160 = 60. If each item were cheaper by 20, the price would be 40 and with Rs 9600 you could buy 9600/40 = 240 items, which is 80 more than 160 (not 40). So 160 does not satisfy the condition.

title: Andre and Betty together weigh pounds. Betty and Chris together
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Andre and Betty together weigh 150 pounds. Betty and Chris together 180 pounds. Andre, Chris and David together weigh 360 pounds. Altogether, the four of them weigh 450 pounds. How much does David weigh?
solution:
Let A, B, C, and D represent the weights of Andre, Betty, Chris, and David respectively.

We are given the total weight of all four people is 450 pounds (A + B + C + D = 450).

We know Andre and Betty weigh 150 pounds together (A + B = 150). Subtracting this from the total gives Chris and David's combined weight: C + D = 450 - 150 = 300 pounds.

We are also told Andre, Chris, and David weigh 360 pounds (A + C + D = 360). Substituting the value of (C + D) found above, we get A + 300 = 360, which means Andre weighs 60 pounds.

Since Andre and Betty weigh 150 pounds, Betty weighs 150 - 60 = 90 pounds.

Since Betty and Chris weigh 180 pounds, Chris weighs 180 - 90 = 90 pounds.

Finally, since Chris and David weigh 300 pounds together, David weighs 300 - 90 = 210 pounds.

title: Find the value of the given expression.
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text:
Find the value of the given expression.

3 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/14 + 2/28
solution:
Concept: fractions can be added only after they are written over one common denominator. Reduce each fraction to lowest terms using a/b = (a ÷ k)/(b ÷ k), rewrite every term over the LCM of the denominators, and then add the numerators. A whole number written beside a fraction denotes their sum; the standard mixed-number form additionally requires that fraction to be proper, so a fractional part whose numerator is at least its denominator must be normalised by carrying the extra whole units into the whole-number part.

Applying this to the given expression 3 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/14 + 2/28:

  1. Reduce the last term to lowest terms: 2/28 = (2 ÷ 2)/(28 ÷ 2) = 1/14, so the expression becomes 3 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/14 + 1/14.

  2. Find the LCM of the denominators 2, 4 and 14. Their prime factorisations are 2 = 2, 4 = 22 and 14 = 2 × 7, so the LCM is 22 × 7 = 28.

  3. Rewrite every fraction over 28: 1/2 = 14/28, 1/4 = 7/28, 1/14 = 2/28 and 1/14 = 2/28.

  4. Add the numerators over the common denominator: (14 + 7 + 2 + 2)/28 = 25/28.

  5. Since 25 is less than 28, the fractional total 25/28 is already a proper fraction, so it stays beside the whole number 3. The expression equals 3 25/28.

Cross-check with decimals: 1/2 = 0.5, 1/4 = 0.25, 1/14 ≈ 0.0714 and 2/28 ≈ 0.0714, and these add to about 0.8929. Since 25/28 ≈ 0.8929, the whole expression is about 3.893, which agrees with the fractional working.

title: In group of cows and hens, the number of legs
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: In a group of cows and hens, the number of legs is 14 more than twice the number of heads. The number of cows is
solution:
Concept

Each animal contributes exactly 1 head, so the head count equals the total number of animals. A hen has 2 legs and a cow has 4 legs. Twice the number of heads counts 2 legs for every animal, so any amount by which the total legs exceed twice the heads must come solely from the 2 extra legs that each cow carries beyond a hen.

Application

  1. Let the number of cows be C and the number of hens be H. Then heads = C + H, and legs = 4C + 2H.

  2. The condition states legs = 2 × (heads) + 14, that is 4C + 2H = 2(C + H) + 14.

  3. Expand the right side: 4C + 2H = 2C + 2H + 14.

  4. Cancel 2H from both sides: 4C = 2C + 14, so 2C = 14.

  5. Divide by 2 to get C = 7. The hen count cancels, so the answer does not depend on how many hens are present.

Cross-check

Take C = 7 and any number of hens, say H = 3. Then heads = 10 and legs = 4(7) + 2(3) = 34. Twice the heads is 20, and 34 − 20 = 14, exactly the required surplus. So 7 cows satisfies the condition for every choice of hens, confirming the result.

It comes from over-stating how much each additional cow changes the gap between the leg total and twice the head count, so fewer cows seem to account for the given difference than actually do. The arithmetic of how the gap grows with each cow has been applied too aggressively here.

This is the number of cows for which the leg total runs ahead of twice the head count by exactly the difference stated in the problem, and it does so whatever the number of hens, since the hens drop out of the comparison entirely. It is the value the condition forces.

This is too high. It results from measuring the legs against the plain head count rather than against twice the head count, which is the comparison the problem actually specifies. Using the wrong baseline makes the apparent difference larger and pushes the cow count up.

title: Volvo bus from Chennai to Bangalore has stops in between.
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A Volvo bus from Chennai to Bangalore has 5 stops in between. At each stop, half of the people will get down. After reaching Bangalore there are only 2 people left out How many people are there on the bus start?
solution:
Key idea: reverse the process. If half the people get off at each stop, then to find the initial number we double the remaining number at each previous step.

  • After reaching Bangalore (after 5 stops): 2 people remain.

  • Before the last stop (one step earlier): 2 × 2 = 4 people.

  • Before the previous stop: 4 × 2 = 8 people.

  • Continue doubling: 8 × 2 = 16 people.

  • Next earlier stop: 16 × 2 = 32 people.

  • Initial number before the first stop: 32 × 2 = 64 people.

Answer: 64 people

title: Pizza boy delivered two-fifths of his pizzas on day three-fourths
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A pizza boy delivered two-fifths of his pizzas on day 1, three-fourths of his pizzas on day 2 and 9/16 of his pizzas on day 3. On which day did he deliver the most pizzas if he had the same number of pizzas in the beginning of each day?
solution:
To determine on which day the pizza boy delivered the most pizzas, compare the fractions of pizzas delivered each day: 2/5, 3/4, and 9/16.

Step 1: Find a common denominator for the fractions. The least common denominator of 5, 4, and 16 is 80.

Step 2: Convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with denominator 80.

2/5 = (2 × 16)/(5 × 16) = 32/80

3/4 = (3 × 20)/(4 × 20) = 60/80

9/16 = (9 × 5)/(16 × 5) = 45/80

Step 3: Compare the numerators: 32, 60, and 45. The largest numerator is 60, which corresponds to 3/4.

Therefore, the pizza boy delivered the most pizzas on Day 2.

Let CP = x. Selling at a 5% loss gives SP = 0.95x. After increasing the selling price by Rs.65, the trader gains 3 1/3%, so the new SP = 31/30 x.

text: A bag is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 23 1/3% of this price, there is a loss of 33 1/3%. What is the percentage profit when it is sold at 56% of the original selling price?
solution:
CONCEPT: In profit-and-loss problems, every selling price must be compared on the cost-price base. If the loss is L%, then selling price = (100 - L)% of cost price; profit percent = (selling price - cost price) / cost price × 100.

APPLICATION:

  1. Let the original selling price be S.

  2. 23 1/3% = 7/30, so the reduced selling price is 7S/30.

  3. A loss of 33 1/3% leaves 66 2/3% = 2/3 of the cost price, so 7S/30 = 2CP/3.

  4. Therefore CP = (7S/30) × (3/2) = 7S/20.

  5. The later selling price is 56% of S = 14S/25.

  6. Profit = 14S/25 - 7S/20 = 56S/100 - 35S/100 = 21S/100.

  7. Profit percent = (21S/100) / (7S/20) × 100 = 60%.

CROSS-CHECK: CP is 35% of S and the later selling price is 56% of S; the gain over the cost base is (56 - 35) / 35 × 100 = 60%.

Result: The profit percentage is 60%.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q65

text: A man sells an article for Rs. 840 at a profit of 20%. If he wishes to make a profit of only 5%, what should be its selling price?
solution:
Concept: The Selling Price (SP) of an article is obtained by adding the profit percentage to its Cost Price (CP): SP = CP × (1 + profit%/100). So the same relation, reversed, recovers the Cost Price from a known Selling Price and profit percentage: CP = SP ÷ (1 + profit%/100). Once CP is known, it stays fixed and can be used to find the Selling Price needed for any other profit percentage.

Application:

  1. Let the cost price of the article be CP.

  2. The article is sold for Rs. 840 at a profit of 20%, so 840 = CP × (1 + 20/100) = CP × 1.20.

  3. Solving for CP: CP = 840 ÷ 1.20 = Rs. 700.

  4. For a profit of only 5%, the required selling price SP2 = CP × (1 + 5/100) = 700 × 1.05.

  5. SP2 = Rs. 735.

Cross-check:

At CP = Rs. 700, a 20% profit gives a profit amount of 700 × 20/100 = Rs. 140, so SP = 700 + 140 = Rs. 840 — matching the selling price given in the question. At a 5% profit, the profit amount is 700 × 5/100 = Rs. 35, so SP = 700 + 35 = Rs. 735, independently confirming the result.

Hence, the selling price should be Rs. 735.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q71
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
subtopic: Finding Profit, Loss, Cost Price, Selling Price, Profit Percent and Loss Percent
text: A man sells 320 mangoes at the cost price of 400 mangoes. His gain percent is
solution:
Concept: When a trader sells fewer articles (say a) at the price that would normally be charged for a larger number of articles (say b, with b greater than a) — that is, the selling price of a articles equals the cost price of b articles — the resulting gain percent follows the identity Gain% = [(b − a) / a] × 100. This holds because the actual cost of the a articles sold is smaller than the cost of b articles, so the cost-value of the extra (b − a) articles becomes the gain earned on the a articles that were actually sold.

  1. Let the cost price of one mango be Rs 1 (a convenient unit, since only the percentage is required).

  2. Cost price of 400 mangoes = 400 × Rs 1 = Rs 400.

  3. The statement says the man sells 320 mangoes at the cost price of 400 mangoes, so Selling Price of 320 mangoes = Rs 400.

  4. Cost Price of the 320 mangoes actually sold = 320 × Rs 1 = Rs 320.

  5. Gain = Selling Price − Cost Price = Rs 400 − Rs 320 = Rs 80.

  6. Gain% = (Gain / Cost Price) × 100 = (80 / 320) × 100 = 25%.

Cross-check: Apply the identity directly with a = 320 and b = 400: Gain% = [(400 − 320) / 320] × 100 = (80 / 320) × 100 = 25%, which matches the step-by-step working above.

optionFeedback.html: A gain of 10% means 10 rupees of profit for every 100 rupees of cost price.
A gain of 15% means 15 rupees of profit for every 100 rupees of cost price.
A gain of 20% means 20 rupees of profit for every 100 rupees of cost price.
A gain of 25% means 25 rupees of profit for every 100 rupees of cost price.

solution:
अवधारणा

विक्रय मूल्य = क्रय मूल्य + लाभ। यह संबंध कुल लेन-देन पर लागू होता है।

प्रयोग

  1. 100 शरीफों का क्रय मूल्य = ₹1200।

  2. 100 शरीफों का कुल विक्रय मूल्य = ₹1200 + ₹800 = ₹2000।

  3. एक दर्जन अर्थात 12 शरीफों का विक्रय मूल्य = ₹2000 × 12 ÷ 100 = ₹240।

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q90

text: A man sold his scooter for ₹9,500, incurring a loss of one-fifth of its selling price. What is the loss percentage (rounded off to the nearest whole number)?
solution:
Concept

For a loss transaction, the cost price equals the selling price plus the loss.

Loss percentage is calculated on cost price: Loss percentage = (loss ÷ cost price) × 100. When loss is given as a fraction of selling price, first find the loss amount and cost price.

Application

  1. Selling price = ₹9,500.

  2. Loss = one-fifth of selling price = (1 ÷ 5) × ₹9,500 = ₹1,900.

  3. Cost price = selling price + loss = ₹9,500 + ₹1,900 = ₹11,400.

  4. Loss percentage = (₹1,900 ÷ ₹11,400) × 100 = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.666…%.

  5. Rounded to the nearest whole number, 16.666…% becomes 17%.

Cross-check

In ratio form, selling price is 5 parts and loss is 1 part, so cost price is 6 parts. Thus the loss is 1 out of 6 parts of cost price, again giving 16.666…%, which rounds to 17%.

Therefore, the loss percentage is 17%.

title: Shopkeeper bought kg of sugar at per kg, kg of
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
subtopic: Multiple Items and Mixed Rate Problems
text: A shopkeeper bought 20 kg of sugar at ₹45 per kg, 25 kg of sugar at ₹50 per kg and 35 kg of sugar at ₹40 per kg. He spent a sum of ₹450 on transportation and other expenses. He mixed all the three types of sugar and sold all the stock at ₹52.50 per kg. His profit per cent in the entire transaction is
solution:
When several batches of the same commodity, bought at different rates, are pooled into one mixed stock and the entire stock is sold at a single uniform price, profit or loss must be worked out on the TOTAL cost versus the TOTAL revenue, not on any one batch's rate. Total Cost Price (CP) = sum of every batch's purchase cost plus any additional expenses (such as transportation); Total Selling Price (SP) = total quantity sold x selling price per unit; Profit % = ((SP - CP) / CP) x 100.

  1. Cost of each batch of sugar: 20 kg x ₹45 = ₹900; 25 kg x ₹50 = ₹1250; 35 kg x ₹40 = ₹1400.

  2. Total cost of the sugar purchased = ₹900 + ₹1250 + ₹1400 = ₹3550.

  3. Add the ₹450 spent on transportation and other expenses: Total Cost Price = ₹3550 + ₹450 = ₹4000.

  4. Total quantity of mixed sugar = 20 + 25 + 35 = 80 kg.

  5. Total Selling Price = 80 kg x ₹52.50 per kg = ₹4200.

  6. Profit = Total SP − Total CP = ₹4200 − ₹4000 = ₹200.

  7. Profit % = (Profit / Total CP) x 100 = (200 / 4000) x 100 = 5%.

Cross-check on a per-kg basis: the weighted-average purchase cost is ₹3550 / 80 kg = ₹44.375 per kg, and the overhead adds ₹450 / 80 kg = ₹5.625 per kg, so the effective cost per kg is ₹44.375 + ₹5.625 = ₹50. Profit per kg = ₹52.50 − ₹50 = ₹2.50, and Profit % = (2.50 / 50) x 100 = 5% — the same result, confirming the answer.

optionFeedback.html: Adding the ₹450 spent on transportation and other expenses to the sugar purchase cost of ₹900 + ₹1250 + ₹1400 = ₹3550 gives a total cost of ₹4000. Selling the full 80 kg mixed stock at ₹52.50 per kg brings in ₹4200, a profit of ₹200 on ₹4000 — exactly 5%.

This is the kind of figure that results from measuring profit against the amount finally collected from selling the mixture rather than against the amount actually spent buying and preparing it for sale — profit percentage must always be worked out on the cost price, never on the selling price.

This is the kind of figure that results from totalling only the cost of the three sugar purchases and leaving the ₹450 spent on transportation and other expenses out of the cost price altogether — every rupee spent to acquire and ready the stock for sale belongs in the cost base.

This is the kind of figure that results from averaging the three purchase rates (₹45, ₹50, ₹40) directly to value the mixed stock instead of weighting each rate by the quantity actually bought at it — a 20 kg batch and a 35 kg batch cannot be given equal weight in the cost calculation.

title: Chair is sold at profit of If the cost price
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A chair is sold at a profit of 30%. If the cost price and selling price were Rs. 720 less, then profit would be 18% more. Find the cost price.
solution:
Concept: When both the cost price (CP) and selling price (SP) of an item are reduced by the same amount, the absolute profit (SP − CP) stays exactly the same — only the profit PERCENTAGE changes, because percentage profit is measured relative to CP, and CP (the base) has shrunk. If CP = x and profit is p%, then SP = x(1 + p/100). Here "profit would be 18% more" is read as 18 percentage points more (30% -> 48%), which is the standard reading in this problem type — confirmed below because it is the only reading that lands on one of the given options.

  1. Let the original cost price be Rs. x. Since the profit is 30%, the original selling price = 1.3x.

  2. Both CP and SP are reduced by Rs. 720: new CP = x − 720, and new SP = 1.3x − 720.

  3. The new profit is 18 percentage points higher than before, i.e. 30% + 18% = 48%. So: (new SP − new CP) / new CP = 48/100.

  4. Substitute: [(1.3x − 720) − (x − 720)] / (x − 720) = 48/100, which simplifies to 0.3x / (x − 720) = 0.48.

  5. Cross-multiply: 0.3x = 0.48x − 345.6, so 0.18x = 345.6, giving x = 1920.

Cross-check: with CP = Rs. 1920, original SP = 1.3 × 1920 = Rs. 2496 (30% profit, confirmed). New CP = 1920 − 720 = Rs. 1200, new SP = 2496 − 720 = Rs. 1776. New profit % = (1776 − 1200)/1200 × 100 = 576/1200 × 100 = 48%, which is indeed 18 percentage points more than 30%. Both conditions hold, confirming the cost price is Rs. 1920. Note also that the absolute profit amount is unchanged at Rs. 576 both before and after (2496 − 1920 = 576 and 1776 − 1200 = 576) — only the percentage rose, because it is now measured against the smaller base of Rs. 1200 instead of Rs. 1920.

optionFeedback.html: With the cost price of Rs. 1920, both conditions hold together: the original selling price of Rs. 2496 reflects the 30% profit, and after reducing both prices by Rs. 720, the new profit works out to exactly 48% -- an 18 percentage-point rise over the original margin.

This value does not satisfy both profit conditions together. A common source of this error is computing the new profit percentage against the original cost price instead of the reduced (new) cost price after both prices drop by Rs. 720.
This value does not satisfy both profit conditions together. A common source of this error is reducing only one of the two prices (cost price or selling price) by Rs. 720 instead of reducing both.

This value does not satisfy both profit conditions together. A common source of this error is adding the 18% increase directly onto the original price relationship instead of forming a fresh profit equation from the reduced cost and selling prices.

title: Study the table and find the ratio
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Study the table and find the ratio P : R .
solution:
Profit percentage is defined as Profit% = ((Selling Price − Cost Price) / Cost Price) × 100. When a cost price is marked up by x% to form the marked price and then a discount of y% is applied to that marked price, the selling price becomes CP × (1 + x/100) × (1 − y/100) — the two percentage changes combine multiplicatively, not by simple addition or subtraction.

  1. Article 1's marked price = 12000 × (1 + 20/100) = 12000 × 1.20 = 14400.

  2. Apply the 10% discount on the marked price: Selling Price M = 14400 × (1 − 10/100) = 14400 × 0.90 = 12960.

  3. Profit percentage P = ((12960 − 12000) / 12000) × 100 = (960 / 12000) × 100 = 8%.

  4. Article 3's marked price = 13000 × (1 + 30/100) = 13000 × 1.30 = 16900.

  5. Apply the 20% discount on the marked price: Selling Price O = 16900 × (1 − 20/100) = 16900 × 0.80 = 13520.

  6. Profit percentage R = ((13520 − 13000) / 13000) × 100 = (520 / 13000) × 100 = 4%.

  7. Ratio P : R = 8 : 4 = 2 : 1.

As an independent check, a mark-up of x% followed by a discount of y% on the marked price is equivalent to one net percentage change of (x − y − xy/100)%. For Article 1: 20 − 10 − (20 × 10)/100 = 8%, which matches P. For Article 3: 30 − 20 − (30 × 20)/100 = 4%, which matches R. So P : R = 8 : 4, which simplifies to 2 : 1.

optionFeedback.html: A ratio written as 2 : 1 means the first term is exactly twice the second term — as a fraction it equals 2, i.e. the first quantity is 200% of the second.
A ratio written as 1 : 2 means the first term is exactly half the second term — as a fraction it equals 0.5, i.e. the first quantity is 50% of the second.
A ratio written as 2 : 3 means the first term is two-thirds of the second term — as a fraction it equals approximately 0.67, i.e. the first quantity is about 66.7% of the second.
A ratio written as 3 : 2 means the first term is one-and-a-half times the second term — as a fraction it equals 1.5, i.e. the first quantity is 150% of the second.
This choice records a non-response — it leaves both profit percentages uncomputed and proposes no numeric relationship between them.

title: The table given below shows the total number of wooden
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text:
The table given below shows the total number of wooden and mechanical pencils in five shops and it also shows the price of total mechanical and wooden pencils.

Shop B sold 20% of wooden pencil at the profit of 20% and rest at the profit of 50%. Find the total selling price of wooden pencil.
solution:
Concept

When two item types share a known total quantity and a known total cost, set up two linear equations — one for quantity (sum of counts) and one for value (price per unit times count) — and solve them simultaneously to recover each count. Then apply each profit rate to the cost of the relevant share: Selling Price = Cost × (1 + profit fraction).

Application

For Shop B the table gives a total of 47 pencils and a total cost of Rs 415, with wooden pencils costing Rs 5 each and mechanical pencils Rs 20 each. Let w be the number of wooden pencils and m the number of mechanical pencils:

  1. Quantity equation: w + m = 47.

  2. Value equation: 5w + 20m = 415.

  3. From the first equation w = 47 − m; substitute into the second: 5(47 − m) + 20m = 415, i.e. 235 + 15m = 415.

  4. So 15m = 180, giving m = 12 and therefore w = 47 − 12 = 35 wooden pencils.

  5. Split the 35 wooden pencils: 20% of 35 = 7 pencils sold at 20% profit; the remaining 35 − 7 = 28 pencils sold at 50% profit.

  6. Selling price = 7 × 5 × 1.20 + 28 × 5 × 1.50 = 42 + 210 = 252.

Hence the total selling price of the wooden pencils is Rs 252.

Cross-check

Verify the counts against the cost data: 5 × 35 + 20 × 12 = 175 + 240 = 415, which matches the table exactly. The cost of the wooden stock is 35 × 5 = Rs 175, so a total selling price of Rs 252 means an overall profit of Rs 77 on the wooden pencils — consistent with a blend of 20% and 50% margins.

optionFeedback.html: 292 results from applying the higher 50% margin to more pencils than the 80% share actually sold at that rate, or from over-counting the wooden pencils in the stock.
215 results from applying the lower 20% margin to most of the stock instead of only to the small 20% share, understating how many pencils were sold at the 50% profit rate.
246 results from rounding the 20% share to a different whole number of pencils, or from a small slip in multiplying one of the cost-times-margin terms.
232 results from mixing up which share carries the 20% margin and which carries the 50% margin, shifting too much stock onto the lower margin.
252 is the total selling price of the wooden pencils. With 35 wooden pencils, 7 are sold at a 20% profit (7 × 5 × 1.20 = 42) and 28 at a 50% profit (28 × 5 × 1.50 = 210), giving 42 + 210 = 252.

title: Person marks his goods above the cost price. He sold
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A person marks his goods 40% above the cost price. He sold 30% of the goods at the marked price, 60% of the goods at a discount of 20%, and the remaining 10% of the goods at a discount of 40%. What is 60% of his overall gain percent?
solution:
Concept: When goods are sold in separate quantity-based batches at different discounts off the same marked price, the overall gain percent equals (total revenue − total cost) ÷ total cost × 100, where each batch's selling price = marked price × (1 − discount%).

  1. Assume total goods = 100 units at a cost price of ₹100 each, so total cost price = ₹10,000. Marked price = 140% of cost price = ₹140 per unit.

  2. Batch 1 — 30 units sold at the marked price: revenue = 30 × ₹140 = ₹4,200.

  3. Batch 2 — 60 units sold at 20% discount on the marked price: selling price = ₹140 × 0.8 = ₹112; revenue = 60 × ₹112 = ₹6,720.

  4. Batch 3 — the remaining 10 units sold at 40% discount on the marked price: selling price = ₹140 × 0.6 = ₹84; revenue = 10 × ₹84 = ₹840.

  5. Total revenue = ₹4,200 + ₹6,720 + ₹840 = ₹11,760. Overall gain = ₹11,760 − ₹10,000 = ₹1,760, so overall gain percent = 17.6%.

  6. The question asks for 60% of the overall gain percent: 0.6 × 17.6% = 10.56%.

Cross-check: each batch's own gain on ₹100 cost is +40% (30 units), +12% (60 units, since ₹112 vs ₹100), and −16% (10 units, since ₹84 vs ₹100). Weighting by quantity share: 0.30×40 + 0.60×12 + 0.10×(−16) = 12 + 7.2 − 1.6 = 17.6%, confirming the overall gain percent and the final value of 10.56%.

title: Medical store owner purchased medicines worth from company. He sold
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: A medical store owner purchased medicines worth ₹6,200 from a company. He sold one-third of the medicines at 33% loss. At what gain should he sell the rest of the medicines, so that he has neither gain nor loss?
solution:
Step-by-Step Solution

To achieve a "neither gain nor loss" (break-even) position, the total profit from the remaining goods must exactly equal the total loss incurred from the first part.

  1. Analyze the first part:

    • Portion of goods = 1/3

    • Loss percentage = 33%

    • Loss amount = (1/3) * 33% = 11% of the total cost price (CP).

  2. Analyze the remaining part:

    • Portion of goods = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3

    • We need this part to generate a profit percentage (P%) that covers the 11% loss.

  3. Set up the equation:

    • Profit from remaining = Loss from first part
